_comment: Cell descriptor for layout/bin/compose-cell.py -- see layout/README.md
for the recipe this follows and layout/bias_core_pnp8_leg/ (issue #30/
PR #33) for the sibling proof cell this recipe was ported from. Issue
#37 (part of #34, itself a follow-on from #30/#4).
This is design/netlist/bias_core.spice's XRT/XR1/XR2/XRZ/XCC/XCOK
device group -- the bias/ratio resistor network (4x
sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po) and Miller compensation caps (2x
sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1) design/bias_core.md describes. 6 devices
total, each its own single-instance klt gen call (`res_array`/
`cap_array` with num=1, dummy=0) rather than a matched array -- unlike
bias_core_pnp8_leg's 8:1 ratio group, none of these 6 devices are
meant to match each other; every one has its own distinct L (or
plate_w_um/plate_h_um) per design/netlist/bias_core.spice.
Floorplan: XR2 (L=4104.0um) is two orders of magnitude longer than
every other device here and dominates this sub-block's bbox --
res_array draws one continuous straight poly body per unit resistor,
with no built-in serpentine/meander folding of a *single* device's own
length (its `rows` param folds separate matched *unit* resistors of an
array into parallel rows, not one long body -- not applicable to a
single L=4104.0 device). placement.strategy 'row' places all 6 blocks
left to right with a uniform gap, so the composed cell's own bbox is
simply as wide as XR2 plus the other 5 devices' combined width --
correct, if large (a multi-millimeter-wide sub-block), rather than
artificially compact.
Connectivity: two of the six devices' terminals are shared within this
device group -- NB (XRT's second node / XR1's first node) and NZ
(XCC's second node / XRZ's first node) -- wired via connectivity[] as
two-pin nets between adjacent row blocks (opposite-facing port pairs,
per docs/cli/gen-compose.md's own obstacle-overlap note). Every other
non-VSS node (NBTOP, EC, VREF, ER, PG, N2, VDD, NOKX) touches exactly
one port within this device group, so each is a `pins[]` declare-only
top-level pin (no metal routed) rather than a connectivity[] net.
VSS: all four resistors' third node is VSS in the design netlist, but
`klt gen res_array` reports only two ports per unit (R<i>_A/R<i>_B) --
the bulk/substrate terminal `sky130_fd_pr__res_xhigh_po` extracts with
(DeviceExtractorResistorWithBulk's synthesized 'vsubs' global) is not a
drawn/routable port at all, so there is nothing in this cell.json to
wire it to a locally-named 'vss' net -- unlike bjt_array's COLL_* ports
(2AMLogic/klayout-tools#1894), which exist but fail to land a contact
when wired. `klt extract` recovers each resistor's bulk on the deck's
global 'vsubs' net instead (shared automatically across all four
devices in this composed cell, with no connectivity[] entry needed).
This turns out NOT to be what blocks LVS below -- the hand-extracted
reference.spice's own device cards already carry VSS as an explicit
third node, so the reference-side device class ends up with the same
3-terminal arity as the layout side once `klt lvs`'s subckt-call
conversion runs (confirmed directly: renaming VSS->vsubs throughout
reference.spice, so the two sides' 11th net is even byte-identical,
does not change the mismatch at all).
KNOWN GAP (both filed generically, see README.md 'Verification' for the
full LVS diagnosis): (1) `klt lvs`'s `form: "subckt-call"` conversion
writes a literal placeholder value '0' for a converted resistor/
capacitor card (by design -- it has no PDK sheet-resistance/
capacitance-per-area table to compute a real one from L=/W=), and
`NetlistComparer` cannot pair ANY device of a class whose every
reference-side instance shares that same placeholder value, collapsing
the whole compare to 'topology: device class could not be mapped to a
counterpart' instead of proceeding on net-topology alone and reporting
the value gap as an ordinary parameter mismatch; (2) `klt extract`'s
own SPICE netlist writer drops a MiM capacitor's device-class/model-
name token from its `C` card entirely (present on every resistor `R`
card, absent on every capacitor `C` card), so a capacitor's class always
reads back as the generic 'CAP', never the specific
'sky130_fd_pr__model__cap_mim' a reference declares -- blocking pairing
independently of (1).
